annotations.annotation_text: The repetitive questioning at the river's darkening edge marks the fading consciousness of the washerwomen as they lose their distinct human identities.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.target_phrase: I feel as old as yonder elm.
annotations.annotation_text: The first explicit stage of metamorphosis where the speaker physically merges with the riparian landscape, turning from washerwoman to tree.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: Swiftian reference linking the washing tub to Jonathan Swift's satire, emphasizing the cyclical purification of history through gossip and laundry.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: Phonetic degeneration of speech into rushing water sounds, reflecting the Liffey's turbulent flow in the dark.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.target_phrase: I feel as heavy as yonder stone.
annotations.annotation_text: The counterpart to the elm metamorphosis; the second washerwoman ossifies into the immovable banks of the Liffey.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.target_phrase: Save me from those therrble prongs!
annotations.annotation_text: Fear of the encroaching darkness and possibly the devil's pitchfork, localized as river debris or menacing branches.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: The quintessential portmanteau of riverine movement, capturing both the physical sloshing and the erratic path of historical recurrence.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: The final word of Book I, completing the transition from the bustling daytime gossip to the unconscious, mythic state of the river's sleep.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org
